messages:
shruti: Alert from infra-scan: found AWS creds mounted in pod filesystem under /etc/config in namespace `payments-staging`. Looks like a legacy k8s secret got mounted into a StatefulSet. Not rotated yet.
security-bot: [automated] Detection: secret-file-exposure (medium) - path=/etc/config/aws-credentials - pod=payment-worker-5 - namespace=payments-staging - detected_by=fs-scan-3
kevin: copying logs, starting triage. Which service account owns that pod?
maria: SA is payments-worker-sa. It has IAM role binding to arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/payments-worker-role.
jen: steps: 1) take pod offline, 2) rotate creds if they are long-lived, 3) patch Helm chart to remove hostPath/secret mount, 4) run audit to find other mounts.
shruti: I ran `kubectl exec` and cat shows plain creds (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET_ACCESS_KEY). Snippet:
```
$ kubectl exec -n payments-staging payment-worker-5 -- cat /etc/config/aws-credentials
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA...ABC
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...verylong...
```
kevin: thanks. First: treat as leaked. I'll open an incident ticket and kick off rotation. @ops-oncall can you create a new IG for the role to block the keys?
ops-oncall: ack, creating temporary deny policy and will detach inline keys from role. ETA 10m.
maria: quick check: are these keys used by external systems? I see CloudWatch put calls from that role earlier today. Might be used by the app only.
jen: rotation plan (short): 1) create new short-lived KMS-encrypted credentials for workload (use IRSA if possible), 2) rotate away the leaked static keys, 3) revoke old keys at AWS, 4) update k8s secret to be KMS-backed via sops or Kustomize with KMS seal, 5) rollout chart with no direct file mounts.
shruti: to be explicit, coords: - Security: rotate & revoke - Platform: remove mount, push chart patch - Infra: restrict SA permissions and add RBAC that prevents non-admins from mounting secrets as files - Dev: update app to use env-based creds from token exchange (IRSA)
kevin: I'll handle AWS rotations. Commands I'll run (for audit):
```
aws iam list-access-keys --user-name payments-worker || true
aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIA...ABC --status Inactive --user-name payments-worker
aws iam delete-access-key --access-key-id AKIA...ABC --user-name payments-worker
```
maria: also adding audit log query to see if creds were exfiltrated externally:
```
# CloudTrail
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=payment-worker-5
```
ops-oncall: deny policy attached, old keys disabled. patch for Helm prepared, removing configVolume and replacing with projected token via IRSA. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/payments/changes/1523
shruti: quick RBAC change proposal to reduce blast radius: allow only `deploy-manager` and `helm-ops` groups to create/update pod specs with hostPath/secret mounts. Everyone else gets deny via OPA constraint. Thoughts?
jen: +1. Also add a cluster audit webhook to flag newly created pods with file mounts that reference secret volumes. Use transient mitigation for 72h.
security-bot: [automated] Audit rule added: pod-secret-file-mounts -> flagged 2 matches in last 24h (payments-staging/payment-worker-4, payments-staging/payment-worker-5).
kevin: I've rotated creds and revoked old keys. Created new IRSA role and updated k8s secret to reference token exchange. Patch rolled to staging. Deleting affected pods now:
```
kubectl rollout restart statefulset/payment-worker -n payments-staging
kubectl delete pod payment-worker-5 -n payments-staging
```
maria: running scan across clusters for similar patterns (searching for files under /etc/config). Will report results in 30m.
shruti: great. Postmortem owners: kevin (rotation), jen (chart & RBAC change), maria (cluster sweep + audit), ops-oncall (deny policy & AWS changes).
jen: we should also create a short-lived incident doc and share to all-hands channel once we have confirmation no external exfiltration.
shruti: noted. Adding retrospective checklist: make all workload creds IRSA or KMS sealed, nightly fs-scan for secret file patterns, and enforce OPA policy.
ops-oncall: done with AWS deny, and monitoring alert set to high for the role.
kevin: closing loop: no suspicious outbound IPs in CloudTrail for that key. marking incident resolved for now, will keep postmortem open. :white_check_mark:
